summary: This Wikipedia-style note profiles Keith Galen Ballard, an American former professional ice hockey defenseman born November 26, 1982. It covers his three seasons at the University of Minnesota's Golden Gophers, his selection by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2002 NHL Entry Draft, and his trades and NHL stints with the Phoenix Coyotes, Florida Panthers and Vancouver Canucks. It also notes his rookie professional season with the Utah Grizzlies in the AHL.
one_line: Keith Ballard is a retired American NHL defenseman who played for Phoenix, Florida, Vancouver and Minnesota after being drafted 11th overall in 2002.
key_facts: Keith Galen Ballard was born on November 26, 1982.
Keith Ballard is an American former professional ice hockey defenseman.
Keith Ballard played in the National Hockey League with the Phoenix Coyotes, Florida Panthers, Vancouver Canucks and Minnesota Wild.
Keith Ballard played college hockey for the Minnesota Golden Gophers of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA) for three seasons.
Keith Ballard was selected 11th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2002 NHL Entry Draft, after his freshman year.
Before making his NHL debut, Keith Ballard was traded initially to the Colorado Avalanche and then to the Phoenix Coyotes.
Keith Ballard played his professional rookie season in 2004–05 with the Utah Grizzlies, the Coyotes' American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate.
Keith Ballard debuted in the NHL with the Phoenix Coyotes the season after his rookie professional season.
After three years with Phoenix, Keith Ballard was traded to the Florida Panthers.
Keith Ballard spent two seasons with the Florida Panthers before being dealt to Vancouver at the 2010 NHL Entry Draft.
